title: K8s resource references as symbol-level edges, not component-level
context: Adding K8s manifest reference resolution (Deployments → ConfigMaps/Secrets, Services → workloads) to the indexer requires deciding whether these references produce symbol-level or component-level graph edges.
decision: Implement K8s resource references as symbol-level 'references' edges (contributing to fan_in/fan_out) rather than component-level 'depends_on' edges. This choice is driven by empirical observation: real Helm charts overwhelmingly co-locate a Deployment and its ConfigMap/Secret in the same templates/ directory, where component-level edges would be filtered out as same-component and produce no signal.
consequences: Symbol-level edges preserve signal for the dominant real-world case of co-located resources
References contribute to fan_in/fan_out metrics, making dependency visibility accurate at scale
Aligns K8s resolution semantics with existing cross-file resolution patterns in the codebase
Requires kind-scoped resolution (not reusing resolveName()) to avoid conflating resources with identical names
alternatives_rejected: Component-level 'depends_on' edges: silently filtered out as same-component in real Helm charts, losing signal
Reusing resolveName() directly: has no concept of Kubernetes kind, would incorrectly conflate ConfigMap and Secret sharing a name

rejected_tripwires.alternative: Component-level 'depends_on' edges: silently filtered out as same-component in real Helm charts, losing signal
Reusing resolveName() directly: has no concept of Kubernetes kind, would incorrectly conflate ConfigMap and Secret sharing a name
